description: The Run Feedback and Costs panels display quality assessments and LLM spend for completed workflow runs. Feedback scores show automated, LLM judge, and manual quality assessments with colored progress bars and expandable reasons. LLM Cost Breakdown shows per-model and per-action cost tables with token counts. Both panels live as tabs within the RunRecapTab tabbed content area. Backend: 8 API endpoints, FeedbackScore and RunCostSummary models, dual PostgreSQL/SQLite storage, TanStack Query hooks with 30-60s staleTime.

architecture.bridge: Agentic metrics auto-push on execution completion (Rust runner -> batch POST -> web backend). Runner completes -> pushScoresToBackend -> batch POST -> FeedbackScore table -> useFeedbackScores hook -> FeedbackScoresPanel

models.FeedbackScore: PostgreSQL â€” id, run_id, name, value (0-1), source (manual|automated|llm_judge), reason, created_at
models.agentic_metric_scores: SQLite + PostgreSQL dual-write for offline resilience
models.RunCostSummary: Aggregated view â€” run_id, total_tokens_input, total_tokens_output, total_cost_usd, llm_action_count, per_model[]
models.ModelCostBreakdown: Per-model row â€” model, provider, tokens_input, tokens_output, cost_usd, action_count

hooks.useFeedbackScores: TanStack Query, 30s staleTime, returns scores[], summary, createScore mutation

groups.name: Feedback Scores Overview
groups.description: The Feedback Scores panel shows all quality assessments at a glance. A summary strip displays the average score and count-by-source badges, followed by individual score rows with colored progress bars (green >= 80%, yellow >= 50%, red < 50%) and source badges (Automated, LLM Judge, Manual). This lets users quickly assess overall run quality without expanding individual scores.

target.label: Average score indicator in summary strip

target.label: Total score count in summary strip

assertions.precondition: The run has at least one feedback score

assertions.description: Each score row displays the score name, a colored progress bar proportional to the 0-1 value, and the score formatted as a percentage (e.g. '85%'). The bar color reflects quality: green (>= 80%), yellow (>= 50%), red (< 50%)

groups.name: Manual Score Creation
groups.description: Users need the ability to manually add feedback scores to a run to capture subjective quality assessments that cannot be computed automatically. Clicking the 'Add Score' button reveals an inline form with name, value (0-1), and optional reason fields. On submission, the score is created via POST /api/v1/feedback-scores with source 'manual' and the form collapses. This is essential for human-in-the-loop quality tracking workflows.

assertions.description: An 'Add Score' button is visible in the panel header (when scores exist) or in the empty state, allowing users to initiate manual score creation
assertions.precondition: At least one workflow run has completed with AI actions

assertions.description: The Add Score action reveals an inline form with fields for Name, Value (0 - 1), and Reason. The Add Score button is replaced with a Cancel button in the header
assertions.precondition: At least one workflow run has completed with AI actions

assertions.description: The Name input field is required, accepts text, and shows placeholder text 'e.g. accuracy' to guide the user on what kind of score names are expected
The Value input field is a number input with min=0, max=1, step=0.01, defaulting to 0.5. The label reads 'Value (0 â€“ 1)' to indicate the valid range
The Reason textarea is optional (label includes '(optional)'), shows placeholder 'Why this score was given...', and allows the user to provide context for the score
The form has a 'Submit' button that is disabled when the name field is empty. Clicking Submit with a valid name creates the score and collapses the form
The form includes a 'Cancel' button that dismisses the form without creating a score. The header also shows a Cancel button (with X icon) that serves the same purpose
While the score creation request is in flight, the Submit button shows a spinner and both Submit and Cancel buttons are disabled to prevent duplicate submissions
preconditions: Score creation mutation is in flight

groups.name: Score Detail Expansion
groups.description: Users need to drill into individual score details to understand the reasoning behind each quality assessment. Score rows that have a reason field are clickable (indicated by a chevron icon) and expand to reveal the reason text with a message icon. Rows without a reason are not interactive. This progressive disclosure keeps the default view clean while allowing detailed investigation.

assertions.description: Score rows with a reason display a right-pointing chevron (collapsed) or down-pointing chevron (expanded) as a visual affordance indicating the row is expandable
preconditions: At least one score has a reason field
assertions.precondition: At least one score has a non-empty reason field

assertions.description: Clicking an expandable score row toggles the expanded state, revealing the reason text in a bordered section below the score bar. The aria-label changes from 'Expand reason for {name}' to 'Collapse reason for {name}'
assertions.precondition: At least one score has a non-empty reason field

assertions.description: When a score row is expanded, the reason text is displayed with a message icon (MessageSquare) in a whitespace-pre-wrap paragraph, preserving any formatting in the original reason text
preconditions: A score row with a reason is expanded
assertions.precondition: At least one score has a non-empty reason field

assertions.description: Score rows without a reason field do not show a chevron and are not clickable (no cursor-pointer, no button role, no aria-label), preventing user confusion about non-expandable rows
preconditions: At least one score has no reason field

groups.name: LLM Cost Breakdown
groups.description: After a run completes, users need to understand how much their LLM usage cost and where the spend went. The LLM Cost Breakdown panel shows a totals strip (total cost, tokens in, tokens out, LLM action count) followed by a per-model breakdown table sorted by cost descending. Each table row shows model name, provider, token counts, cost in USD, and action count. This helps users optimize their model selection and identify cost-heavy steps.

assertions.description: The totals strip shows 'Tokens Out' with the formatted total output token count (comma-separated), letting users gauge response sizes across the run

groups.name: Tab Navigation
groups.description: The Feedback Scores and LLM Costs panels are accessed via tabs in the RunRecapTab tabbed content area. Users need to discover and navigate to these tabs alongside the existing tabs (Timeline, Verification, Knowledge, Context, Canvas, Diffs & Replay, Errors). Each tab has an icon and label. Correct tab routing ensures the right panel renders with the current run's data.

assertions.description: A 'Feedback Scores' tab trigger is visible in the tab list with a BarChart3 icon, and clicking it activates the feedback tab content area containing the FeedbackScoresPanel
An 'LLM Costs' tab trigger is visible in the tab list with a DollarSign icon, and clicking it activates the LLM costs tab content area containing the RunCostBreakdown
The FeedbackScoresPanel receives the current taskRunId as its runId prop, ensuring scores are fetched for the correct execution run when the tab is activated
The RunCostBreakdown receives the current taskRunId as its runId prop, ensuring cost data is fetched for the correct execution run when the tab is activated
The default active tab is 'timeline', not 'feedback' or 'llm-costs', so users see the run timeline first and navigate to feedback/costs tabs intentionally

groups.name: Data Display Formatting
groups.description: Verifies that feedback scores and cost data are displayed with correct formatting, proportional sizing, and sort order. Score progress bars must reflect the 0-1 value scale. Numeric values must follow their respective formatting rules (percentages, dollar amounts, comma-separated tokens).

assertions.description: Score progress bars have width proportional to the score value on a 0-1 scale, computed as `${Math.max(score.value * 100, 2)}%` with a 2% minimum so zero-value scores remain visible
Score values are formatted via formatScore as `${(value * 100).toFixed(0)}%`, rendering as an integer percentage (e.g. 0.85 -> '85%') in a tabular-nums span
Cost values are formatted via formatCost with a dollar sign: `$${usd.toFixed(2)}` for costs >= $0.01, or `$${usd.toFixed(4)}` for sub-cent amounts (e.g. '$1.23' or '$0.0045')
Token counts in both the TotalsStrip and ModelRow are formatted via formatTokens using count.toLocaleString(), which inserts comma separators for thousands (e.g. 1234567 -> '1,234,567')
The per-model breakdown rows are sorted by cost_usd descending via `[...data.per_model].sort((a, b) => b.cost_usd - a.cost_usd)`, so the most expensive model appears first

target.label: Model rows in descending cost order

groups.name: State Consistency
groups.description: Verifies that derived/aggregated values displayed in the UI are mathematically consistent with the underlying data. Summary averages must match computed averages, badge counts must match filtered score counts, and cost totals must reconcile with per-model breakdowns.

assertions.description: The average score displayed in the SummaryStrip (formatScore(summary.averageScore)) matches the mathematical average of all displayed scores: sum(scores.map(s => s.value)) / scores.length

Each source badge in the SummaryStrip shows a count (e.g. 'Automated (3)') that equals the number of scores in the scores array with that source: scores.filter(s => s.source === source).length, rendered only when count > 0
The 'Total Cost' value in the TotalsStrip (formatCost(data.total_cost_usd)) matches the sum of all per-model costs: data.per_model.reduce((sum, m) => sum + m.cost_usd, 0)

For each ModelRow, tokens_input + tokens_output equals the total tokens for that model. Across all models, the sums match the TotalsStrip: data.per_model.reduce((sum, m) => sum + m.tokens_input, 0) === data.total_tokens_input and data.per_model.reduce((sum, m) => sum + m.tokens_output, 0) === data.total_tokens_output

target.label: Total token counts vs per-model sums
